target: Harganya masih boleh ditawar sedikit, Bu?
english: Can the price still be bargained down a little, ma'am?
tip: di- flips who acts: ditawar = get bargained; harganya boleh ditawar = the price can be haggled.

target: Wah, masih kemahalan, Pak.
english: Wow, that is still way too expensive, sir.
tip: ke-...-an makes 'too X': mahal → kemahalan = too expensive, overpriced.

target: Turunkan sedikit, Pak, nanti saya ambil dua pasang.
english: Lower it a little, sir, and I will take two pairs.
tip: -kan makes 'cause to': turun = go down, turunkan = lower it. Turunkan harganya!

target: Ini harga pas, tidak bisa kurang lagi.
english: This is a fixed price, it cannot go down any more.
tip: harga pas = fixed price — the seller's polite signal that bargaining is over.

target: Ya sudah, khusus untuk Ibu, dua ratus ribu saja.
english: Alright then, just for you, ma'am, only two hundred thousand.
tip: Ya sudah = alright then — the giving-in phrase: Ya sudah, dua ratus ribu saja.

target: Jangan malu menawar kalau berbelanja di pasar tradisional.
english: Do not be shy about bargaining when you shop at a traditional market.
tip: menawar = to haggle; menawarkan = to offer. Saya menawar harganya = I bargained over the price.

target: Bisa bayar pakai QRIS di sini?
english: Can I pay with QRIS here?
tip: QRIS (say: kris) is the QR code payment used everywhere: bayar pakai QRIS.

target: Uangnya sudah saya transfer ke rekening kamu tadi pagi.
english: I already transferred the money to your account this morning.
tip: Put the thing first for done deals: uangnya sudah saya transfer = the money, I already sent.

target: Boleh minta nota untuk laporan kantor saya?
english: May I ask for a receipt for my office report?
tip: nota = handwritten receipt from small shops; struk = the printed one.

target: Ini kembaliannya lima puluh ribu, silakan dihitung dulu.
english: Here is your change, fifty thousand, please count it first.
tip: kembalian = your change, from kembali (come back): Ini kembaliannya.

target: Maaf Mbak, kembaliannya kurang lima ribu.
english: Sorry, miss, the change is five thousand short.
tip: Mbak politely addresses a young woman: Maaf, Mbak = excuse me, miss.

target: Simpan kembaliannya untuk parkir nanti sore.
english: Keep the change for parking later this afternoon.
tip: -nya works like 'the': kembalian = change, kembaliannya = the change we both know about. Simpan kembaliannya = keep the change.

target: Kartu ATM saya tertelan di mesin kemarin sore.
english: My ATM card got swallowed in the machine yesterday afternoon.
tip: ter- often means 'by accident': tertelan = got swallowed. Kartu saya tertelan.

target: Saldo saya tinggal dua ratus ribu sampai gajian.
english: My balance is only two hundred thousand left until payday.
tip: tinggal usually means live, but with amounts it means left: saldo saya tinggal dua ratus ribu = my balance is down to 200,000.

target: Pulsa saya habis, jadi tidak bisa menelepon.
english: My phone credit has run out, so I cannot make calls.
tip: habis = used up, and it stands alone as the whole statement: pulsa saya habis = my credit ran out. No extra verb needed.

target: Tolong isikan pulsa ke nomor ibu saya, ya.
english: Please top up credit for my mother's number, okay?
tip: isikan = fill it for someone: isikan pulsa ke nomor ini = top up this number.

target: Paketnya tiba dalam tiga hari kalau pakai kilat.
english: The package arrives within three days if you use express.
tip: kilat = lightning: pos kilat = express mail. Kalau pakai kilat = if you use express.

target: Paket dari ibu saya belum sampai juga.
english: The package from my mother still has not arrived.
tip: Pending things take belum, not tidak: belum sampai = hasn't arrived yet. Tidak sampai would mean it's not coming at all – belum says you still expect it.

target: Boleh saya pinjam uang lima puluh ribu sampai besok?
english: May I borrow fifty thousand until tomorrow?
tip: Boleh asks permission, bisa is ability. Boleh saya pinjam uang? = may I borrow money? Use boleh when you need a yes from someone.

target: Kakak meminjamkan uang ke saya untuk membeli buku kuliah.
english: My older sibling lent me money to buy college books.
tip: meminjam = borrow, meminjamkan = lend: meminjamkan uang ke saya = lent money to me.

target: Struknya mau dibawa, Kak?
english: Would you like the receipt, miss?
tip: Struknya mau dibawa? is the stock checkout question – cashiers ask it at nearly every register. struk = receipt; answer Mau (yes please) or Tidak usah (no need).

target: Di struk ini ada diskon sepuluh persen, lumayan.
english: There is a ten percent discount on this receipt, not bad.
tip: lumayan = not bad, pretty good — the word for pleasant surprises: Diskonnya lumayan!

target: Saya menukar dolar di money changer dekat hotel.
english: I exchange dollars at the money changer near the hotel.
tip: Indonesians say money changer; tempat penukaran uang is the formal sign version.

target: Titip beli sabun di minimarket ya, uangnya nanti.
english: Please buy me soap at the minimarket, okay, I will give you the money later.
tip: titip = ask someone to bring or get something: Titip beli sabun, ya = please get me soap.

target: Rapat sore ini mundur satu jam, ya.
english: This afternoon's meeting is pushed back one hour, okay?
tip: For meetings, mundur = pushed later: rapat mundur satu jam = the meeting moved back an hour.

target: Rapat besok maju jadi jam delapan pagi.
english: Tomorrow's meeting is moved up to eight in the morning.
tip: maju means go forward, and on a schedule forward = earlier: rapat maju jadi jam delapan = the meeting moved up to eight. The opposite, postponed, is diundur.

target: Klien minta rapat diundur ke minggu depan.
english: The client asked for the meeting to be postponed to next week.
tip: di- = done to it: diundur = postponed (by someone) — rapat diundur ke minggu depan.

target: Pak Hasan, apakah Bapak bisa hadir di rapat jam tiga?
english: Mr. Hasan, can you attend the three o'clock meeting, sir?
tip: Formal: use the title instead of kamu — apakah Bapak bisa hadir? = can you attend, sir?

target: Deadline laporan ini hari Kamis jam lima sore.
english: The deadline for this report is Thursday at five in the afternoon.
tip: Office speech uses deadline; tenggat is its formal written synonym.

target: Kirim datanya paling lambat besok siang, ya.
english: Send the data by tomorrow noon at the latest, okay?
tip: paling lambat besok siang = by tomorrow noon at the latest. Its partner is paling cepat (at the earliest) – the pair brackets any deadline window.
